Title: Building partnerships for better brain health
NewsSummary: Prof. Valcour's visit deepens collaboration in dementia research

content.text: The Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) hosted Prof. Victor Valcour, Director of the Global Brain Health Institute (GBHI) at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), for a series of engagements on October 14-15, 2025, focused on strengthening research and training in brain health across the region.

During his visit, Prof. Valcour delivered a public lecture titled Accompaniment in Brain Health Research: Leveraging the Teachings of Paul Farmer for Sustainable Impact. Drawing on his global experience, he spoke about the principle of "accompaniment" working with communities rather than for them, as essential to building trust and ensuring that research leads to real-world change.

"True partnership in brain health means walking with communities, not ahead of them," said Prof. Valcour. "By building local capacity, we ensure that the impact of research extends far beyond the lab, into the lives of those we aim to serve."

Prof. Valcour also led a hands-on training for BMI researchers on neurological examination techniques, aimed at strengthening local expertise in the diagnosis and assessment of neurological conditions. The session aligned with BMI's wider efforts to build regional capacity in brain health research and practice.

The visit was part of the 'Building Research Infrastructure to Develop Global Expertise' (BRIDGE) Africa Project, a collaboration between GBHI and BMI that seeks to advance research and capacity in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias across East Africa. The project is guided by the belief that progress in dementia science must be grounded in local realities and cultural contexts.

Reflecting on the collaboration, Prof. Zul Merali, Founding Director of BMI, highlighted the need for a holistic approach to dementia research, one that integrates science with care and community support.

"Caring for the brain also means caring for those who provide care," said Prof. Merali. "Research on dementia helps us understand not only the disease but also how to support caregivers and improve outcomes for families."

The engagement reaffirmed a shared commitment between GBHI and BMI to advance collaborative, inclusive brain health research. Through sustained partnerships and knowledge exchange, the two institutions are nurturing a new generation of researchers and practitioners dedicated to improving brain health outcomes across Africa and beyond.
